name: Paul Cézanne
findings: Within his own canvases, yellowish brown turns up as a small accent in 80% of the paintings that hold it, 3.1x the archive's rate (from 757 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, chapman's blue turns up as the lightest note in 60% of the paintings that hold it, 2.8x the archive's rate (from 757 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, rood's brown turns up as the shadow in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 2.5x the archive's rate (from 757 paintings here).
Rarely uses smoky black, common in the same museum(s)' other paintings (from 757 paintings here).
Rarely uses dark olive brown, common in the same museum(s)' other paintings (from 757 paintings here).
Pairs pale cerulean with pastel blue more than chance would predict (3 of 757 paintings here).
Pairs dark sienna with dark chocolate brown more than chance would predict (3 of 757 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, dark jungle green, black) covers 67% of his paintings here.
